classification.difficultyReason: Account for how the transferred colour changes the second box, construct weighted paths or equally likely transfer-and-draw outcomes, and combine the black outcomes.

content.prompt: A box contains 3 black and 1 yellow ball. A second box contains 2 black and 2 yellow balls. A ball is taken from the first box and put in the second. A ball is then withdrawn from the second box. Find the probability that the ball taken from the second box is:

answer.short:
$\frac{11}{20}$

Label the balls and count 11 black outcomes among 20 equally likely transfer-and-draw outcomes.
answer.worked:
Label the first box's balls $B_1,B_2,B_3,Y$. Label the second box's four original balls $b_1,b_2,y_1,y_2$, and call the transferred ball $t$.

Record each outcome as (transferred ball, ball drawn). Each of the four equally likely transfers has five equally likely draws: $b_1,b_2,y_1,y_2,t$. Thus there are 20 equally likely outcomes.

The outcomes giving a black draw are:
$$\begin{gathered}(B_1,b_1),\ (B_1,b_2),\ (B_1,t),\\(B_2,b_1),\ (B_2,b_2),\ (B_2,t),\\(B_3,b_1),\ (B_3,b_2),\ (B_3,t),\\(Y,b_1),\ (Y,b_2).
\end{gathered}$$
There are 11 favourable outcomes out of 20.
$$P(\text{black from second box})=\frac{11}{20}$$

Black and yellow are complementary outcomes.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{yellow from second box})&=1-P(\text{black from second box})\\P(\text{yellow from second box})&=1-\frac{11}{20}\\P(\text{yellow from second box})&=\frac9{20}\end{align*}$$
